title: The Billboard on the Highway
subtitle: The Sodder Children · West Virginia, 1945
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, Appalachian West Virginia hills in late December 1945, cold dormant deciduous forest, frost, dim winter light, smoke-grey sky, rural two-lane highway, melancholy and uncanny, period 1945 detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: On Christmas night, nineteen forty-five, a fire destroyed the Sodder family home in the West Virginia hills.
beats.img: A weathered 1940s rural American wooden farmhouse at night seen from a distance, cold dim winter light, bare deciduous trees, faint smoke rising from the roof line, isolated and melancholy, no people, nothing graphic.

beats.vo: Five of the ten Sodder children were never seen again.
beats.cap:

beats.vo: No bones were found in the ashes. A coroner issued death certificates without remains.
beats.img: A low pile of grey ash and charred timber in the snow where a house stood, cold winter morning light, melted snow around the wreckage, desolate, no people, nothing graphic.

beats.vo: Twenty-two years later, a photograph arrived in the mail. The family believed it showed their son Louis, in his twenties.
beats.img: A single aged photograph lying on a worn wooden kitchen table, blurry, indistinct face, period 1960s domestic background, warm documentary light, melancholy, no recognizable person.

beats.vo: The billboard stood by the highway for forty years. No explanation was ever confirmed.
beats.img: A weathered wooden roadside billboard on a rural American two-lane highway in winter, faded, seen from a distance across a brown dormant field, bare trees, overcast sky, melancholy and unresolved, no people.
